steps.inversions: An inversion puts another note of the chord at the bottom, and it’s still the same chord. With the root at the bottom it’s in root position; with the third, first inversion; with the fifth, second inversion. Here’s {cMajor} in first inversion.
steps.onKeys: Three keys of a chord are lit. Which of its notes is at the bottom?
steps.gap: On the staff, a stack of thirds is root position. Otherwise, look for the gap of a fourth: the root is the note just above it. At the top of the chord it’s first inversion; at the bottom, second inversion.
steps.onStaff: Find the gap, then name the inversion.
steps.build: Now build them, from the lowest note up. The name tells you which note goes at the bottom.
steps.minor: Minor chords invert the same way.
